input: Run a KYC screen on Greensill Capital in the United Kingdom

output.risk_rationale: High risk as of 2026-11-09. The screened entity is GREENSILL CAPITAL (UK) LIMITED, the group's main UK operating company, not its Australian parent or German bank. It remains in administration, and its registered PSC and former director, Alexander David Greensill, accepted a nine-year director-disqualification undertaking following misconduct involving the UK company and a $440 million loss to a Credit Suisse fund (adverse_media[0–1]). Historical fraud allegations, continuing civil proceedings and political connections add risk, although allegations, disclosure obligations and settlements are not findings of criminal liability. No exact-name OFAC SDN match or UK/EU Greensill-name listing was established; broader OFAC fuzzy candidates remain unresolved, and the underlying trust ownership has not been fully identified, so this is not sanctions clearance. Companies House lists no current directors or secretaries; the administrators control the company. GLEIF records LEI 2138004D9J9DZUANAI93 as LAPSED: https://www.gleif.org/lei/2138004D9J9DZUANAI93. One entity-mismatched finding was excluded: the FCA investigation into Mirabella's oversight of Greensill Capital Securities, not this company. Missing fields: registry numbers for the Australian parent and German bank; nationalities of the administrators. Underlying trust beneficiaries/trustees, definitive PEP classification and developments after the dated litigation updates were not established. All screening counts and current-status assessments are as of 2026-11-09; historical amounts and events retain their stated dates.

adverse_media.status: Final disqualification undertaking accepted on 2026-06-02; nine-year ban effective from 2026-06-23, running until June 2035. Court action ended through the undertaking rather than a completed trial.
adverse_media.summary: The Insolvency Service reported that Lex Greensill caused Greensill companies to enter Katerra transactions removing protections for a Credit Suisse fund. He also caused or allowed the screened UK company to use $440 million received in November 2020 for purposes other than redeeming the relevant notes, resulting in a $440 million loss to the fund. The conduct breached his director's duty of reasonable care, skill and diligence.

adverse_media.status: Administration remains recorded as of 2026-11-09. The administrators' report states that the administration was extended to 2028-09-07.
adverse_media.summary: The screened UK company entered administration on 2021-03-08. It is an insolvent entity under insolvency-officeholder control, not an ordinary operating counterparty.

adverse_media.status: Settled litigation; notice of voluntary dismissal with prejudice filed on 2022-08-02. The reviewed record does not establish an adjudicated fraud finding.
adverse_media.summary: Bluestone Resources and associated plaintiffs sued the UK company, Lex Greensill and Roland Hartley-Urquhart. The complaint alleged contractual breaches, fraud and material misrepresentations concerning financing and repayment arrangements. These were plaintiffs' allegations, not proven facts.

adverse_media.status: The official SFO case page is labelled Open; its latest listed investigative activity is dated 2022-04-27. No charge or criminal finding against the screened company was established from the reviewed source.
adverse_media.summary: The SFO investigation concerns suspected fraud, fraudulent trading and money laundering involving GFG Alliance companies, including their financing arrangements with Greensill Capital UK Ltd. The investigation's stated targets are GFG businesses; this is not a finding that the screened company committed those offences.
adverse_media.category: Criminal investigation connected to financing arrangements

adverse_media.status: According to the report covering the period to 2026-09-07, the English proceedings were stayed after a jurisdiction judgment in GCUK's favour on 2026-02-04. Related Australian security proceedings were deferred to November 2026; later developments were not established.
adverse_media.summary: GFG commenced English proceedings against GCUK, Greensill Bank and UBS concerning a financing/security dispute. The administrators also pursued Australian proceedings to determine the validity of GCUK's security over relevant Liberty entities. These are civil recovery and security disputes, not criminal findings.

adverse_media.status: Status date in the administrators' report: GCUK was an inactive party in Australian insurance proceedings and joined to English investor–insurer proceedings. The English claim was stayed against GCUK except for discovery. Later developments were not established.
adverse_media.summary: The screened company remains involved in post-collapse insurance litigation and document disclosure. Its participation is directly established, but the report does not establish a liability judgment against it.

adverse_media.status: As at the administrators' reporting date, GCUK was joined as a defendant and providing discovery. No merits determination against GCUK was established; later developments were not verified.
adverse_media.summary: Greensill Bank brought proceedings against the Secretary of State for Business and Trade concerning CBILS/CLBILS investments and underlying guarantees. GCUK was joined because it was the accredited lender and was required to provide disclosure.

citations.title: Lessons from Greensill Capital: Sixth Report of Session 2021–22 — Treasury Committee
excerpts: The Greensill group sat outside the Bank’s regulatory perimeter and as such was not subject to prudential regulation by the PRA. The holding company, Greensill Capital Pty Limited, was registered in Australia, although its main operating entity, Greensill Capital (UK) Limited was incorporated in England and Wales. This operating entity did not carry out any activities regulated by the Bank under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (FSMA). The group also owned a bank, Greensill Bank AG, which was domiciled and regulated in Germany and was not authorised to perform any regulated activities in the UK.87

excerpts: 39\. Lex Greensill, the founder of Lex Capital, also held roles in Government. From 2012 to 2015 he was an adviser to David Cameron’s Government. Although there was apparently no contract and he was unpaid, he was given a security pass for both the Cabinet Office and Downing Street, as well as a business card stating that he was an adviser with direct contact details for Number 10 Downing Street, which would certainly give the impression of having a formal role within Government. citations.title: Filing History
excerpts: As updated in the Prior Period, immediately prior to the commencement of GCUK’s IB Proceedings, GFG commenced a Part 7 application against GCUK, GBAG and UBS in the Commercial Court in England on 22 September 2025; in breach of GCUK’s statutory moratorium which was not permitted to be lifted. Accordingly, the Joint Administrators defended the proceedings and following an interlocutory hearing to determine jurisdiction, judgment was delivered in GCUK’s favour on 4 February 2026 ruling that the dispute should be determined in the Australian courts. As such, the English proceedings commenced by GFG are stayed until the outcome of the IB Proceedings.

English insurance proceedings GCUK remains joined to two English insurance court proceedings between investors and insurers. The claim is currently stayed against GCUK for all purposes other than discovery, and the Joint Administrators have agreed the receipt of cost contributions towards its discovery per court orders dated 22 November 2024. During the Period, GCUK has continued to work with its legal advisors regarding documents available for discovery, as instructed by the Court, and commence the discovery process. As with the Australian proceedings, we continue to update the Committee on the progress of the proceedings. We expect the majority of this discovery work to complete in the Following Period.

CBILS/CLBILS GBAG has issued legal proceedings against the Secretary of State for Business and Trade in respect of its CBILs and CLBILs investments and underlying guarantees. GCUK (as the accredited lender of the CBILs and CLBILs) has been joined as a defendant to those proceedings and we are required to provide discovery. The disclosure process has continued in the Period, and we anticipate the majority of this discovery work will be completed in the Following Period. We continue to ensure that, to the extent possible, GCUK’s reasonable costs of providing disclosure are paid for by GBAG.

basis.reasoning: The sources establish the disqualification, insolvency, complaint and dismissal, financing-related investigation and specific civil proceedings involving the UK company. The answer separates admissions and outcomes from allegations and dates the civil-status information to the administrators' reporting period.

citations.title: Lex Greensill to be disqualified from acting as a company director in the UK for nine years - GOV.UK
excerpts: From: [The Insolvency Service](https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/insolvency-service) Published: 4 June 2026

Lex Greensill caused the three Greensill companies to enter transactions that removed the legal protections underpinning the Credit Suisse fund’s investment in late 2020. The transactions meant that the receivables no longer required payment, security held against those receivables was released, and the payment obligations supporting the fund’s trade credit insurance were cancelled. The transactions were entered into without the written consents required. Lex Greensill also caused or allowed Greensill Capital (UK) Limited to use $440 million received in November 2020 for purposes other than redeeming the notes owed to the Credit Suisse fund. The notes all defaulted when they fell due, resulting in a loss of $440 million to the Credit Suisse fund. His conduct breached his legal duty under the Companies Act 2006 to exercise reasonable care, skill and diligence as a company director.

A six-week trial was due to begin on Monday 8 June, but Lex Greensill signed a disqualification undertaking – a legally-binding agreement where directors do not dispute certain facts (for the purposes of the disqualification proceedings only) to end court action. The disqualification undertaking was accepted by the Secretary of State for Business and Trade on Tuesday 2 June and his ban comes into effect on Tuesday 23 June.
Financier to be banned until June 2035
Lex Greensill will be banned as a company director in the UK for nine years after agreeing to be disqualified following an investigation by the Insolvency Service.
